q-114870.name: Question 1
q-114870.worked_solution:
The denominator of the integrand doesn't divide the numerator exactly, so we need to decompose it into its quotient and remainder. For this, we can use synthetic division.

We start by drawing up our synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ 3 & 6 & 5 \\  & ↓ & 18 \\  & 6 & 23\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{6x+5}{x-3}=6+\frac{23}{x-3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{6x+5}{x-3}\,\text{d}x & =\int (6+\frac{23}{x-3})\text{d}x \\  & =6\int \text{d}x+23\int \frac{1}{x-3}\,\text{d}x \\  & =6x+23\operatorname{ln}⁡|x-3|+C.\end{aligned}
$$

We first need to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder parts, which we can do using synthetic division.

We draw up a synthetic division table:

$$
\begin{aligned} & {x}^{2} & {x}^{1} & {x}^{0} \\ 5 & 1 & -11 & 15 \\  & ↓ & 5 & -30 \\  & 1 & -6 & -15\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}-11x+15}{x-5}=x-6-\frac{15}{x-5}.
$$

Therefore,

$$

q-352244.name: Question 9
q-352244.worked_solution:
The denominator of the integrand doesn't divide the numerator exactly, so we need to decompose it into its quotient and remainder. For this, we can use synthetic division.

We start by drawing up our synthetic division table:

|  | ${x}^{2}$ | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $-2$ | $1$ | $7$ | $4$ |
|  | $↓$ | $-2$ | $-10$ |
|  | $1$ | $5$ | $-6$ |

So, from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\frac{{x}^{2}+7x+4}{x+2}=x+5-\frac{6}{x+2}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{{x}^{2}+7x+4}{x+2}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{1}^{3}(x+5-\frac{6}{x+2})\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{1}^{3}x\,\text{d}x+5{\int }_{1}^{3}\text{d}x-6{\int }_{1}^{3}\frac{1}{x+2}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{1}^{3}+5x\,{|}_{1}^{3}-6\operatorname{ln}⁡|x+2|\,{|}_{1}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({3}^{2}-{1}^{2})+5(3-1)-6(\operatorname{ln}⁡|3+2|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|1+2|) \\  & =4+10-6(\operatorname{ln}⁡5-\operatorname{ln}⁡3) \\  & =14-6\operatorname{ln}⁡(\,\frac{5}{3}\,).\end{aligned}
$$

q-114896.name: Question 11
q-114896.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $6$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{6x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{6(x+\frac{1}{6})}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{6})}\,\text{d}x.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

$$
\begin{aligned} & x & {x}^{0} \\ -\frac{1}{6} & 2 & 1 \\  & ↓ & -\frac{1}{3} \\  & 2 & \frac{2}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

So from the synthetic division, we get that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+1}{(x+\frac{1}{6})} & =2+\frac{(\frac{2}{3})}{(x+\frac{1}{6})} \\  & =2+\frac{4}{6x+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{2x+1}{6x+1}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}(2+\frac{4}{6x+1})\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[2{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\text{d}x+4{\int }_{-1/12}^{0}\frac{1}{6x+1}\,\text{d}x] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[2x+\frac{4}{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡|6x+1|]}_{-1/12}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[2x+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡|6x+1|]}_{-1/12}^{0} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[2(0-(-\frac{1}{12}))+\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|6(0)+1|-\operatorname{ln}⁡|6(-\frac{1}{12})+1|)] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[2(\frac{1}{12})+\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡1-\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{1}{2}))] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\frac{1}{6}+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡2] \\  & =\frac{1}{36}(1+4\operatorname{ln}⁡2).\end{aligned}
$$

q-347424.worked_solution:
First, we pull out the factor of $3$ from the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7x-2}{3x+1}\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7x-2}{3(x+1/3)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}\frac{7x-2}{(x+1/3)}\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we draw up our synthetic division table to decompose the integrand into its quotient and remainder.

|  | ${x}^{1}$ | ${x}^{0}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $-\frac{1}{3}$ | $7$ | $-2$ |

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7x-2}{(x+1/3)} & =7-\frac{(13/3)}{(x+1/3)} \\  & =7-\frac{13}{3x+1}.\end{aligned}

$$
